questions.question: In what year did the United Nations General Assembly adopt the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) in Paris?
questions.explanation: The UDHR was adopted on December 10, 1948, now celebrated globally each year as Human Rights Day.

questions.question: What is the foundational assertion of Article 1 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?

options.label: A
options.text: 'All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights'

options.label: B
options.text: 'All citizens must serve in the armed forces'

options.label: C
options.text: 'Rights belong only to property owners'

options.label: D
options.text: 'Freedom of speech is subject to government approval'

questions.correct_answer_text: 'All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights'
questions.explanation: Article 1 famously proclaims that all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights, endowed with reason and conscience.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as a fundamental human right under the UDHR?

options.label: A
options.text: Freedom from torture and cruel, inhuman treatment

options.label: B
options.text: Unrestricted right to pollute public rivers

options.label: C
options.text: Right to evade legitimate tax laws

options.label: D
options.text: Right to discriminate based on skin color

questions.correct_answer_text: Freedom from torture and cruel, inhuman treatment
questions.explanation: Article 5 of the UDHR categorically prohibits torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment.

questions.question: Why are human rights described as 'inalienable'?

options.label: A
options.text: Because they cannot be legitimately taken away or surrendered by any person or authority

options.label: B
options.text: Because they only apply to foreign visitors

options.label: C
options.text: Because they expire when a person turns sixty

options.label: D
options.text: Because they must be purchased annually

questions.correct_answer_text: Because they cannot be legitimately taken away or surrendered by any person or authority
questions.explanation: 'Inalienable' means impossible to take away, transfer, or give up; every human being possesses them inherently by virtue of being human.

questions.question: What is the synonym of the word 'dignity' in the context of universal human rights?

options.label: A
options.text: Inherent self-worth and honor

options.label: B
options.text: Material wealth

options.label: C
options.text: Political power

options.label: D
options.text: Physical arrogance

questions.correct_answer_text: Inherent self-worth and honor
questions.explanation: 'Dignity' refers to the state or quality of being worthy of universal honor, respect, and fundamental human consideration.

topics.topic_name: Amerigo - Plight of a Street Child

questions.question: How old is Amerigo, the street child whose poignant first-person story is featured in 'English for Today'?

options.label: A
options.text: 13 years old

options.label: B
options.text: 8 years old

options.label: C
options.text: 18 years old

options.label: D
options.text: 21 years old

questions.correct_answer_text: 13 years old
questions.explanation: Amerigo begins his account by stating: 'My name is Amerigo. I am 13 years old and I live on the street, alone.'

questions.question: Why does Amerigo live alone on the harsh streets of Dhaka city?

options.label: A
options.text: His parents are separated; his mother told him to go away and his father refused to accept him

options.label: B
options.text: He chose to live outdoors for fun

options.label: C
options.text: He is attending a distant boarding school

options.label: D
options.text: He is employed as a hotel manager

questions.correct_answer_text: His parents are separated; his mother told him to go away and his father refused to accept him
questions.explanation: Amerigo's mother remarried and abandoned him, while his impoverished father refused to send bus fare or take custody of him.

questions.question: What dangerous job did Amerigo do at a trash dump that caused him serious illness?

options.label: A
options.text: Collecting trash and sorting recyclable plastics, which gave him severe infections

options.label: B
options.text: Driving heavy garbage trucks

options.label: C
options.text: Selling electronic gadgets

options.label: D
options.text: Operating an incinerator machine

questions.correct_answer_text: Collecting trash and sorting recyclable plastics, which gave him severe infections
questions.explanation: He worked at a hazardous trash dump until he fell terribly sick from infected cuts and was warned by a doctor to stop.

questions.question: What heartbreaking injustice did Amerigo experience while working at an ice cream shop on the beach?

options.label: A
options.text: The shop owner made him carry heavy ice cream boxes all day but gave him only stale food and no wages, not even letting him taste an ice cream

options.label: B
options.text: He dropped an ice cream and was arrested

options.label: C
options.text: Customers refused to buy ice cream from him

options.label: D
options.text: The ice cream shop burned down

questions.correct_answer_text: The shop owner made him carry heavy ice cream boxes all day but gave him only stale food and no wages, not even letting him taste an ice cream
questions.explanation: Amerigo carried heavy boxes across the beach, yet the cruel vendor gave him no money and forbade him from tasting even a single ice cream.

questions.question: In winter, what happened to Amerigo's friend who collected trash?

options.label: A
options.text: He died of a severe infection and tetanus from a rusted nail in a trash heap

options.label: B
options.text: He was adopted by a wealthy foreign family

options.label: C
options.text: He moved to a warm village home

options.label: D
options.text: He became a primary school teacher

questions.correct_answer_text: He died of a severe infection and tetanus from a rusted nail in a trash heap
questions.explanation: Amerigo recounts the sorrowful death of his young friend who stepped on a rusted glass/nail in the garbage pile and died without medical care.

topics.topic_name: Child Rights and Child Labor Exploitation

questions.question: Which international treaty protects the fundamental rights of every human under eighteen years of age?

options.label: A
options.text: UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)

options.label: B
options.text: Geneva Maritime Convention

options.label: C
options.text: Kyoto Protocol

options.label: D
options.text: World Intellectual Property Treaty

questions.correct_answer_text: UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)
questions.explanation: The UNCRC (1989) is the most widely ratified human rights treaty, guaranteeing children's rights to health, education, protection, and family care.

questions.question: What basic childhood rights is Amerigo deprived of in his day-to-day existence?

options.label: A
options.text: Right to shelter, education, nutritious food, healthcare, and parental love

options.label: B
options.text: Right to travel on international airlines

options.label: C
options.text: Right to own commercial real estate

options.label: D
options.text: Right to drive high-speed automobiles

questions.correct_answer_text: Right to shelter, education, nutritious food, healthcare, and parental love
questions.explanation: Amerigo suffers total deprivation of essential rights guaranteed by the UNCRC: a secure home, formal education, medical care, and family protection.

questions.question: What is the primary root cause driving millions of young children into hazardous labor in developing countries?

options.label: A
options.text: Extreme poverty, parental illiteracy, and lack of social safety nets

options.label: B
options.text: Excessive academic homework in primary schools

options.label: C
options.text: Desire to purchase expensive luxury sports cars

options.label: D
options.text: Boredom with extracurricular leisure sports

questions.correct_answer_text: Extreme poverty, parental illiteracy, and lack of social safety nets
questions.explanation: Grinding socio-economic poverty forces vulnerable families to send young children into hazardous manual labor to survive.

questions.question: What does Amerigo fear the most when winter approaches in Dhaka?

options.label: A
options.text: Freezing cold nights on pavement without warm clothes or blankets

options.label: B
options.text: Missing school examinations

options.label: C
options.text: Snow avalanches in the streets

options.label: D
options.text: Having too much food to eat

questions.correct_answer_text: Freezing cold nights on pavement without warm clothes or blankets
questions.explanation: Amerigo shivers through winter nights on bare sidewalks, lacking warm clothing, blankets, or shelter against biting winds.

questions.question: What is society's collective moral obligation toward street children like Amerigo?

options.label: A
options.text: Providing rehabilitation, free education, healthcare, and safe shelter to integrate them into society

options.label: B
options.text: Chasing them away from public view

options.label: C
options.text: Imposing police fines on them

options.label: D
options.text: Ignoring their plight completely

questions.correct_answer_text: Providing rehabilitation, free education, healthcare, and safe shelter to integrate them into society
questions.explanation: Governments and civil societies have an urgent moral and constitutional duty to rehabilitate, educate, and protect vulnerable homeless children.

topics.topic_name: Peace and Conflict - Concepts and Typologies

questions.question: What is the definition of 'Conflict' in sociological studies?

options.label: A
options.text: A clash or disagreement between individuals or groups arising from opposing interests, values, or needs

options.label: B
options.text: A harmonious choir singing in unison

options.label: C
options.text: A formal treaty signed between allies

options.label: D
options.text: An agricultural harvest festival

questions.correct_answer_text: A clash or disagreement between individuals or groups arising from opposing interests, values, or needs
questions.explanation: Conflict occurs when two or more parties perceive incompatible goals, values, territorial claims, or access to scarce resources.

questions.question: How do peace researchers differentiate between 'Negative Peace' and 'Positive Peace'?

options.label: A
options.text: Negative peace is merely the absence of direct violence, while positive peace is the presence of social justice and equality

options.label: B
options.text: Negative peace is war, positive peace is defeat

options.label: C
options.text: There is no difference between them

options.label: D
options.text: Negative peace applies only to wildlife

questions.correct_answer_text: Negative peace is merely the absence of direct violence, while positive peace is the presence of social justice and equality
questions.explanation: Johan Galtung formulated that negative peace means ceasing active warfare, while positive peace dismantles structural violence and injustice.

questions.question: Which of the following is a major root cause of interstate or international conflict?

options.label: A
options.text: Territorial disputes, resource competition (oil, water), and ideological hostility

options.label: B
options.text: Mutual international cultural exchange programs

options.label: C
options.text: Joint scientific research in astronomy

options.label: D
options.text: Universal adherence to humanitarian laws

questions.correct_answer_text: Territorial disputes, resource competition (oil, water), and ideological hostility
questions.explanation: Clashes over borders, vital natural resources, political dominance, and ethnic grievances drive most major interstate conflicts.

questions.question: What is an 'Intrapersonal Conflict'?

options.label: A
options.text: A psychological struggle or moral dilemma occurring within an individual's own mind

options.label: B
options.text: A boxing match between two professional athletes

options.label: C
options.text: A trade tariff dispute between two sovereign nations

options.label: D
options.text: A strike organized by a labor union

questions.correct_answer_text: A psychological struggle or moral dilemma occurring within an individual's own mind
questions.explanation: Intrapersonal conflict takes place internally within a person's consciousness between competing ethical values, emotions, or decisions.

questions.question: Which diplomatic mechanism is standardly used by sovereign nations to resolve conflicts peacefully?

options.label: A
options.text: Mediation, multilateral dialogue, and arbitration

options.label: B
options.text: Unilateral nuclear missile strikes

options.label: C
options.text: Targeted assassination of civilian populations

options.label: D
options.text: Imposition of total media blackouts

questions.correct_answer_text: Mediation, multilateral dialogue, and arbitration
questions.explanation: Peaceful conflict resolution relies on diplomatic negotiations, neutral third-party mediation, and international judicial arbitration (ICJ).

topics.topic_name: Non-violent Resistance and Global Peace Builders

questions.question: Who pioneered the philosophy of 'Satyagraha' (non-violent resistance through soul-force) to win India's independence?

options.label: A
options.text: Mahatma Gandhi

options.label: B
options.text: Subhas Chandra Bose

options.label: C
options.text: Jawaharlal Nehru

options.label: D
options.text: Bhagat Singh

questions.correct_answer_text: Mahatma Gandhi
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi developed Satyagraha (holding onto truth without violence), inspiring civil rights movements across the globe.

questions.question: Which American civil rights leader was deeply inspired by Gandhi to lead the Montgomery Bus Boycott and the March on Washington?

options.label: A
options.text: Martin Luther King Jr.

options.label: B
options.text: Malcolm X

options.label: C
options.text: Frederick Douglass

options.label: D
options.text: Booker T. Washington

questions.correct_answer_text: Martin Luther King Jr.
questions.explanation: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. adopted Gandhi's non-violent civil disobedience methods to fight racial segregation in the United States.

questions.question: Which Catholic nun dedicated her life to serving the destitute, dying, and lepers on the streets of Kolkata, winning the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979?

options.label: A
options.text: Mother Teresa

options.label: B
options.text: Florence Nightingale

options.label: C
options.text: Sister Nivedita

options.label: D
options.text: Joan of Arc

questions.correct_answer_text: Mother Teresa
questions.explanation: Mother Teresa founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata to minister selflessly to the poorest of the poor, sick, and dying.

questions.question: Martin Luther King Jr. declared: 'Injustice anywhere is a threat to ______.'

options.label: A
options.text: Justice everywhere

options.label: B
options.text: Commercial trade agreements

options.label: C
options.text: Military superiority

options.label: D
options.text: Government revenue

questions.correct_answer_text: Justice everywhere
questions.explanation: In his 'Letter from Birmingham Jail' (1963), King wrote: 'Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere. We are caught in an inescapable network of mutuality.'

questions.question: What is the core premise of non-violent civil disobedience?

options.label: A
options.text: Refusing to obey unjust, discriminatory laws openly and peacefully while accepting legal penalties to awaken society's conscience

options.label: B
options.text: Organizing armed guerilla insurgencies in forests

options.label: C
options.text: Destroying public infrastructure under cover of darkness

options.label: D
options.text: Fleeing the country as a political fugitive

questions.correct_answer_text: Refusing to obey unjust, discriminatory laws openly and peacefully while accepting legal penalties to awaken society's conscience
questions.explanation: Non-violent resistance relies on moral conviction, boycotts, and peaceful marches to expose the injustice of oppressive laws.

questions.question: Who is the legendary village storyteller in R.K. Narayan's story 'Under the Banyan Tree'?

options.label: A
options.text: Nambi

options.label: B
options.text: Swami

options.label: C
options.text: Mani

options.label: D
options.text: Raju

questions.correct_answer_text: Nambi
questions.explanation: Nambi is the venerable, illiterate village elder who lives in the temple hut and enchants villagers with mesmerizing stories under the banyan tree.

questions.question: How did Nambi signal to the villagers of Somal that a new story was ready to be told?

options.label: A
options.text: By lighting a small clay brass lamp in the niche of the banyan tree trunk

options.label: B
options.text: By beating a loud brass gong through village streets

options.label: C
options.text: By sending handwritten invitations

options.label: D
options.text: By shouting from the temple roof

questions.correct_answer_text: By lighting a small clay brass lamp in the niche of the banyan tree trunk
questions.explanation: Whenever inspired by the goddess Shakti, Nambi lit a small lamp on the trunk of the banyan tree, alerting villagers to gather at nightfall.

questions.question: Where does the story of Nambi take place in Narayan's fictional literary universe?

options.label: A
options.text: Somal, a secluded forest village near Malgudi

options.label: B
options.text: A coastal port town in Bombay

options.label: C
options.text: An industrial coal town in Bihar

options.label: D
options.text: A Himalayan monastery in Sikkim

questions.correct_answer_text: Somal, a secluded forest village near Malgudi
questions.explanation: The story is set in Somal, a quiet, simple village tucked deep in the forests of Narayan's iconic fictional region of Malgudi.

questions.question: What heartbreaking crisis struck Nambi in his old age when he attempted to narrate a story?

options.label: A
options.text: His memory faltered, words failed him, and he could no longer weave tales

options.label: B
options.text: The villagers threw stones at him

options.label: C
options.text: The banyan tree was struck by lightning

options.label: D
options.text: The temple was taken over by merchants

questions.correct_answer_text: His memory faltered, words failed him, and he could no longer weave tales
questions.explanation: In his twilight years, Nambi lost his gift of storytelling: words evaporated, his narrative broke down, and he sat in helpless silence.

questions.question: What profound decision did Nambi make after realizing that the divine goddess had withdrawn her gift of words?

options.label: A
options.text: He took a vow of lifelong silence, declaring that when the goddess takes back her speech, the storyteller must remain silent

options.label: B
options.text: He moved to a big city to earn money

options.label: C
options.text: He began reading from printed paper books

options.label: D
options.text: He cursed the villagers in anger

questions.correct_answer_text: He took a vow of lifelong silence, declaring that when the goddess takes back her speech, the storyteller must remain silent
questions.explanation: Nambi gracefully embraced silence: 'It is the Mother who gives the gift, and it is she who takes it away. What is left for the storyteller except silence?'

topics.topic_name: Vocabulary of Peace, Justice and Conflict

questions.question: What is the synonym of the word 'atrocity' in human rights violations?

options.label: A
options.text: An extremely cruel, heinous, or barbaric act

options.label: B
options.text: A peaceful charitable gesture

options.label: C
options.text: A routine administrative disagreement

options.label: D
options.text: A celebration of sportsmanship

questions.correct_answer_text: An extremely cruel, heinous, or barbaric act
questions.explanation: 'Atrocity' refers to an appalling, horrifyingly wicked or cruel act, especially during wartime or ethnic cleansing.

questions.question: What does the word 'disenfranchised' mean in socio-political rights?

options.label: A
options.text: Deprived of basic legal, civil, or political rights and privileges

options.label: B
options.text: Awarded an honorary academic certificate

options.label: C
options.text: Granted commercial franchise ownership

options.label: D
options.text: Exempted from all personal taxes

questions.correct_answer_text: Deprived of basic legal, civil, or political rights and privileges
questions.explanation: 'Disenfranchised' describes marginalized people who have been stripped of power, civil voice, or the right to vote.

questions.question: What is an agreement between warring factions to temporarily stop fighting called?

options.label: A
options.text: Truce (or Ceasefire)

options.label: B
options.text: Ultimatum

options.label: C
options.text: Siege

options.label: D
options.text: Conscription

questions.correct_answer_text: Truce (or Ceasefire)
questions.explanation: A truce or ceasefire is a formal mutual suspension of armed hostilities for negotiation or humanitarian purposes.

questions.question: What is the antonym of the word 'belligerent'?

options.label: A
options.text: Peaceable and amicable

options.label: B
options.text: Aggressive and combative

options.label: C
options.text: Hostile and fierce

options.label: D
options.text: Antagonistic

questions.correct_answer_text: Peaceable and amicable
questions.explanation: 'Belligerent' means hostile, aggressive, and eager to fight. Its direct antonym is 'peaceable' or 'amicable'.

questions.question: What does 'sovereignty' signify for an independent nation?

options.label: A
options.text: Supreme and independent political authority over its own territory and population

options.label: B
options.text: Subservience to colonial rulers

options.label: C
options.text: Requirement of foreign approval for national laws

options.label: D
options.text: Bankruptcy of the central treasury

questions.correct_answer_text: Supreme and independent political authority over its own territory and population
questions.explanation: 'Sovereignty' is the absolute, autonomous power of a state to govern its domestic affairs without foreign intervention.

topics.topic_name: Grammar and Syntax in Rights-Based Texts

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: 'Amerigo was deprived ______ a normal childhood and basic education.'

options.label: A
options.text: of

options.label: B
options.text: from

options.label: C
options.text: with

options.label: D
options.text: in

questions.correct_answer_text: of
questions.explanation: The appropriate preposition after the verb 'deprive' is 'of' (deprived of something).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence in subjunctive mood expressing a human rights imperative:

options.label: A
options.text: The United Nations recommends that every child be protected from hazardous labor.

options.label: B
options.text: The United Nations recommends that every child is protected from hazardous labor.

options.label: C
options.text: The United Nations recommends that every child was protected from hazardous labor.

options.label: D
options.text: The United Nations recommends that every child will protect from hazardous labor.

questions.correct_answer_text: The United Nations recommends that every child be protected from hazardous labor.
questions.explanation: Verbs of recommendation and demand (recommend, demand, insist) take the subjunctive base form 'be protected'.

questions.question: 'Amerigo wishes he ______ a warm family and a secure roof over his head.'

options.label: A
options.text: had

options.label: B
options.text: has

options.label: C
options.text: have

options.label: D
options.text: is having

questions.correct_answer_text: had
questions.explanation: Unreal present wishes after 'wish' require the past subjunctive form ('had').

questions.question: Transform into passive: 'The shopkeeper denied Amerigo his rightful wages.'

options.label: A
options.text: Amerigo was denied his rightful wages by the shopkeeper.

options.label: B
options.text: His rightful wages denied Amerigo by the shopkeeper.

options.label: C
options.text: Amerigo had denied by the shopkeeper.

options.label: D
options.text: The shopkeeper was denied by Amerigo.

questions.correct_answer_text: Amerigo was denied his rightful wages by the shopkeeper.
questions.explanation: In passive transformation, the indirect object 'Amerigo' becomes the subject: 'Amerigo was denied his rightful wages by the shopkeeper.'

questions.question: 'Neither poverty nor abandonment ______ crushed Amerigo's yearning for life.'

options.label: A
options.text: has

options.label: B
options.text: have

options.label: C
options.text: are

options.label: D
options.text: were

questions.correct_answer_text: has
questions.explanation: Both subjects linked by 'neither... nor...' are singular ('poverty', 'abandonment'), so the singular verb 'has' is required.

questions.question: What is the official definition of a 'Refugee' under the 1951 Refugee Convention?

options.label: A
options.text: A person forced to flee their country owing to a well-founded fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality, or political opinion

options.label: B
options.text: A person traveling abroad on holiday vacation

options.label: C
options.text: A student studying at a foreign university

options.label: D
options.text: A businessman visiting a foreign trade fair

questions.correct_answer_text: A person forced to flee their country owing to a well-founded fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality, or political opinion
questions.explanation: The 1951 Geneva Convention defines refugees as individuals who cannot return home due to well-founded fear of violence or persecution.

questions.question: Which United Nations agency is tasked with protecting and aiding displaced refugees worldwide?

options.label: A
options.text: UNHCR (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees)

options.label: B
options.text: IMF (International Monetary Fund)

options.label: C
options.text: WTO (World Trade Organization)

options.label: D
options.text: FIFA

questions.correct_answer_text: UNHCR (United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees)
questions.explanation: UNHCR is the global UN agency mandated to aid and protect refugees, forcibly displaced communities, and stateless people.

questions.question: What is the crucial humanitarian principle of 'Non-Refoulement'?

options.label: A
options.text: Host nations must not forcibly return refugees to a territory where they face serious threats to their life or freedom

options.label: B
options.text: Refugees must never learn the host nation's language

options.label: C
options.text: Refugees cannot be provided with food rations

options.label: D
options.text: Refugees must pay a tax to leave a camp

questions.correct_answer_text: Host nations must not forcibly return refugees to a territory where they face serious threats to their life or freedom
questions.explanation: The cornerstone principle of international refugee law prohibits expelling or returning refugees to countries where they would face danger or persecution.

questions.question: Bangladesh set an extraordinary global humanitarian example in 2017 by doing what?

options.label: A
options.text: Sheltering over a million displaced Rohingya refugees fleeing ethnic cleansing in Myanmar

options.label: B
options.text: Building a massive wall across all land borders

options.label: C
options.text: Banning international humanitarian aid agencies

options.label: D
options.text: Declaring war on neighboring nations

questions.correct_answer_text: Sheltering over a million displaced Rohingya refugees fleeing ethnic cleansing in Myanmar
questions.explanation: Bangladesh opened its borders to provide refuge and humanitarian shelter to over one million persecuted Rohingyas fleeing Myanmar.

questions.question: What international body based at The Hague prosecutes individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes?

options.label: A
options.text: International Criminal Court (ICC)

options.label: B
options.text: Universal Postal Union

options.label: C
options.text: International Civil Aviation Organization

options.label: D
options.text: World Meteorological Organization

questions.correct_answer_text: International Criminal Court (ICC)
questions.explanation: The ICC is the permanent international court established under the Rome Statute to prosecute individuals for grave international crimes.

questions.question: Amerigo states, 'I always want to go to sleep in my own bed at home.' What does this poignant line reveal?

options.label: A
options.text: His deep, natural yearning for domestic security, parental warmth, and a home

options.label: B
options.text: That he owns a luxury bedroom in the city

options.label: C
options.text: That he is too lazy to work

options.label: D
options.text: That he dislikes walking

questions.correct_answer_text: His deep, natural yearning for domestic security, parental warmth, and a home
questions.explanation: The line exposes the emotional wound of every displaced street child whose most basic childhood desire is the security and comfort of home.

questions.question: What is the moral significance of Nambi's quiet dignity in R.K. Narayan's story?

options.label: A
options.text: He accepts the natural cycle of life with humility, refusing to fake a divine gift he no longer possesses

options.label: B
options.text: He tries to deceive the villagers to make money

options.label: C
options.text: He leaves his village out of shame

options.label: D
options.text: He blames his listeners for being impatient

questions.correct_answer_text: He accepts the natural cycle of life with humility, refusing to fake a divine gift he no longer possesses
questions.explanation: Nambi models ultimate spiritual integrity: when inspiration ceases, he honors silence rather than degrading his craft into hollow trickery.

questions.question: How does social conflict within a community damage economic and educational development?

options.label: A
options.text: It destroys trust, disrupts schools, causes physical devastation, and diverts scarce resources to warfare

options.label: B
options.text: It accelerates industrial productivity

options.label: C
options.text: It lowers the national cost of living

options.label: D
options.text: It doubles university enrollment

questions.correct_answer_text: It destroys trust, disrupts schools, causes physical devastation, and diverts scarce resources to warfare
questions.explanation: Armed strife and civil unrest destroy civic infrastructure, shutter educational institutions, and force budget diversions into destruction.

questions.question: Which core value is essential for transforming hostile communities into peaceful societies?

options.label: A
options.text: Mutual empathy, active listening, and restorative justice

options.label: B
options.text: Vindictive vengeance and retaliation

options.label: C
options.text: Total denial of historical wrongs

options.label: D
options.text: Forced exile of losing parties

questions.correct_answer_text: Mutual empathy, active listening, and restorative justice
questions.explanation: Lasting peace requires acknowledging past trauma, practicing empathy, and establishing fair, inclusive social systems.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'culture of peace' actively promote?

options.label: A
options.text: Values, attitudes, and behaviors based on non-violence, human rights, tolerance, and dialogue

options.label: B
options.text: Expansion of military arsenals

options.label: C
options.text: Censorship of literature

options.label: D
options.text: Isolation from neighboring nations

questions.correct_answer_text: Values, attitudes, and behaviors based on non-violence, human rights, tolerance, and dialogue
questions.explanation: The UN defines a culture of peace as a way of life anchored in non-violence, democratic participation, human rights, and global solidarity.
